title: Provision and Passage
premise: Elodie Galloway, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Vane brothers—lenders whose optimism is more dangerous than their violence—takes one last contract chasing storms across the Corren Range. There, a dying prospector named Hask trades her a map to an abandoned silver claim in exchange for a promise: deliver his ledger of stolen wages to the miners' widows before the passes close. The map is also the collateral the Vane brothers want, and they send collectors after her. Elodie must choose between selling the map to clear her debt and keeping her promise, crossing the range ahead of the snows with the collectors closing in. In the end she burns the map rather than surrender it, pays her debt with the storm-chasing contract money instead, and finds that belonging came not from the claim but from the people who waited for Hask's ledger.
about_author: Casper Marchetti is the pen name of a former backcountry guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through the northern ranges before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people outrunning their debts, both financial and moral.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Chasing a supercell across the flats, Elodie calculates fuel, debt, and distance—the arithmetic of never stopping. The Vane brothers' collector, Rill, catches up at a fuel depot and gives her until first snowfall. That night she finds Hask collapsed on the road, silver-dust in his lungs, and he offers the map for a promise. Emotional beat: exhaustion sharpening into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: A Promise Priced in Silver
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Studying the map, Elodie realizes its value could erase her debt entirely—and that Rill will know what she carries. She begins the ascent anyway, following Hask's marked route past ghost camps where miners once worked claims that were never paid out. A rockslide destroys her chase rig, stranding her on foot. Emotional beat: the growing pull between self-preservation and the promise.

chapters.title: What the Collectors Carry
chapters.summary: POV alternates Elodie and Rill as both race the weather line. Rill corners her at a waystation; instead of fighting, he reveals the Vane brothers already sold Hask's claim rights twice over—the map is worthless except as leverage against them. Elodie realizes justice won't come from the law or the ledger alone but from delivering it publicly. They cross the high pass as the storm breaks. Emotional beat: enemy becoming uneasy ally; resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Provision and Passage
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Half-frozen, she reaches the valley settlement and reads Hask's ledger aloud to the assembled widows—names, wages, dates—turning paper into testimony. When Vane's men arrive demanding the map, she feeds it into the stove and lets the ledger stand in its place. She settles her own debt with honest contract money and stays through winter, teaching the settlement to read the sky. Emotional beat: arrival, release, and belonging earned by choice.
